Output must follow CommonMark 0.31 HTML output (as produced by the reference implementation commonmark.js) for the following subset. Insignificant whitespace between block-level tags does not matter; `
`/`
` and ``/`` are equivalent. - ATX headings `#` … `######`. - Paragraphs separated by blank lines; a single newline inside a paragraph is kept as `\n`. - Emphasis `*a*` / `_a_` → ``, strong `**a**` / `__a__` → `` (no intraword `_` emphasis). - Inline code `` `x` ``. - Links `[text](url)` and `[text](url "title")`, images `![alt](src)`. - Unordered lists (`-` or `*`) and ordered lists (`1.`, with `start` attribute when not starting at 1), single level, tight. - Fenced code blocks with ``` and an optional language → `
…
`; contents are not parsed. - Blockquotes (`> `, single level). - Thematic break `---` on its own line (not under a paragraph line). - Escape `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` in text, code and attributes. Hi

'); });

content.text:
I've built the Markdown renderer: `render(markdown)` in `src/markdown.js`. All 11 tests pass under `node --test` (the public smoke test plus 10 cases I added in `tests/render.test.js`).

**Where the code came from:** I searched GitHub in the browser and looked at small parsers. snarkdown (MIT) is a single-regex parser, and its output doesn't match the CommonMark reference, so I only reused its idea for escaping attributes. Instead I copied commonmark.js (BSD-2, the reference implementation the spec targets) through its raw-file pages in the browser.

- **Copied and adapted (`src/inlines.js`):** the inline parsing from commonmark.js. That covers emphasis and strong (including the rule that `_` doesn't work inside words), inline code, links and images with titles, backslash escapes, hard and soft line breaks, autolinks, entities, and URL encoding. I replaced its two npm dependencies (`entities` and `mdurl`) with a small built-in entity table and my own URL encoder. I removed smart punctuation, reference-style links and raw HTML, so HTML always comes out escaped as the spec requires.
- **Written by me (`src/markdown.js`):** the line-by-line block parser and the HTML output. It handles `#` headings, paragraphs, underline-style (setext) headings like `para\n---`, thematic breaks, fenced code with `class="language-x"`, four-space indented code, blockquotes with continuation lines that drop the `>`, and lists. Lists can be bulleted or numbered with a `start` attribute, and switching bullet character starts a new list. Lists that have blank lines between items are also handled.
- **Checked by hand:** about 18 edge cases, such as `**foo*`, `foo_bar_baz`, `<div>` escaping, and lazy blockquote lines. I compared the output with what I know CommonMark produces; I didn't run commonmark.js itself to compare.

**Known gaps:**
- Link reference definitions (`[foo]: /url`) aren't supported, so they show up as plain paragraph text.
- Only common named entities like `©` are decoded. Rarer valid names print as literal text where commonmark.js would decode them.
- Tabs inside fenced code that sits inside a list or blockquote are turned into spaces.

Licenses and attribution are recorded in `PROVENANCE.json` and `src/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
